title: SQL injection in product search
description: The search term is concatenated directly into a SQL LIKE expression instead of being bound as a parameter. An unauthenticated caller can alter the WHERE clause.
evidence: GET /products/search?q=%27%20OR%201%3D1-- returned HTTP 200 and all six catalogue products, demonstrating predicate bypass.

title: Stored SQL injection in staff review report
description: reviews_by_customer interpolates customer display_name into SQL. A customer can set this through PATCH /account and a staff report request then executes the resulting SQL fragment.
evidence: PATCH /account accepts punctuation in display_name; GET /admin/reports/reviews?customer_id=... reaches the f-string at lines 77-81 without parameterization.

title: Persistent cross-site scripting in product reviews
description: Review bodies are stored without HTML sanitization and rendered with Jinja's safe filter. Any authenticated user can persist markup that executes for product-page visitors.
evidence: POST /products/<product_id>/reviews accepts body up to 2000 characters at products.py:82-92, and product.html line 13 emits r.body|safe.

title: Unauthenticated pickle deserialization of basket cookie
description: The basket cookie is client-controlled and unsigned, yet passed to pickle.loads. A crafted cookie can invoke attacker-controlled pickle reductions during any basket-reading request, resulting in code execution.
evidence: read_basket decodes request.cookies['basket'] and calls pickle.loads at line 20; with_basket only base64-encodes pickle data and provides no signature.

title: Authenticated users can view other customers' orders
description: show_order calls get_order, which selects solely by order ID, rather than own_order. A signed-in user who guesses another order ID can retrieve status, totals, items, and refund history.
evidence: GET /orders/<order_id> is protected only by require_auth at lines 46-49; get_order lines 25-29 has no customer_id predicate, while IDs are sequential.

title: Trailing-slash refund route bypasses staff authorization
description: The admin authorization hook compares request.path to exact route rules. The refunds route allows a trailing slash, so /admin/refunds/ is accepted but does not equal the collected /admin/refunds rule; the handler runs without staff authorization.
evidence: Unauthenticated POST /admin/refunds/ reached the refund handler and returned HTTP 404 {"error":"no such order"} rather than 403. With a valid order it can call issue_refund without checking g.user.

title: Payment timeout is treated as successful payment
description: When provider status times out, confirm_payment assigns status='paid' and transitions the order to processing with paid_pence equal to the order total. An outage or induced timeout therefore marks an order paid without confirmation.
evidence: The requests.Timeout handler at lines 39-42 assigns paid; lines 43-46 update status to processing and paid_pence to total_pence.

title: Hardcoded JWT signing secret permits token forgery
description: SECRET_KEY is a fixed repository-visible string used as the HS256 key for bearer JWTs. Anyone obtaining source can mint tokens with arbitrary user IDs and claims, bypassing authentication and authorization.
evidence: config.py line 3 sets SECRET_KEY to a fixed string; auth.py lines 27 and 42 use it to sign and validate HS256 tokens.

title: Passwords stored as unsalted fast SHA-256 hashes
description: Password hashes are plain SHA-256 digests with no salt or work factor. Database disclosure permits rapid offline dictionary and brute-force recovery.
evidence: hash_password at lines 15-16 is hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest(), and registration stores it directly at line 78.
